source: Package creation is not approval of review-history transfer. Thomas must explicitly approve any A successor before replaces is activated. All C cards stay active.

rows.reason: The old prompt declares Präteritum universally mandatory for police/accident reports. The new card explicitly qualifies the ordinary written-event-report convention. A corrected scope is not an exact history match.

The old prompt combines seven W questions, style, chronology, tenses and a dated accident example. These are distributed and qualified in the new lessons; no single successor preserves the complete retrieval.
The same atomic retrieval is preserved: Präsens for a generally applicable process description.
The old prompt combines materials, chronology, tense, four address forms and specialist vocabulary. The new tasks split this knowledge and do not preserve the entire old retrieval.
The same atomic retrieval is preserved: the term for grammatically inflectable word classes.

The old five-main-class taxonomy and its long analysis are not the new atomic word-class retrieval. The lesson distinguishes word class from adverbial function and preserves no whole multi-part successor.
The same atomic retrieval is preserved: Plusquamperfekt formed with hatte/war and Partizip II.

The old retrieval combines all six forms of lesen with a rigid rule about anteriority. The package teaches the forms and temporal relationships separately; no complete identical retrieval is preserved.
The old wording calls a sentence constituent indivisible and describes the displacement test as unconditionally reliable. The new lesson qualifies the test and checks meaning and grammar.
The old retrieval combines analysis methods, all core constituents, four adverbial types and a complete sample analysis. New lessons divide these into separate retrievals.
The same atomic retrieval is preserved: the meaningful dieses/jenes/welches substitution test.
The old retrieval combines s spelling, das/dass, nominalisation and nested-clause punctuation. These are separate lessons and cards; one review history cannot be spread across them.
